text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the cause of your jaundice and pruritus, have you noticed any abdominal pain, particularly in the upper right side? Also, have you experienced any recent fever or chills?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the painless jaundice and significant weight loss, I am concerned about a malignancy such as pancreatic cancer. To clarify the history, did you experience any unintentional weight loss prior to these two weeks, and have you noticed any new-onset diabetes or changes in your bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and weight loss, I need to check for signs of malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan is unexpected given the symptoms, so I need to look closer at the biliary tree. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP demonstrates marked dilation of the common bile duct measuring 1.5 cm in diameter. There is an abrupt cutoff of the distal common bile duct with no filling defect visualized at the site of obstruction. The intrahepatic bile ducts are also dilated. The pancreatic duct appears normal in caliber.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abrupt cutoff of the common bile duct without a visible mass on CT or MRCP raises suspicion for cholangiocarcinoma or ampullary carcinoma. To better visualize the ampulla and rule out a small tumor, I will request direct visualization. REQUEST TEST: ERCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ERCP demonstrates a stricture at the ampulla of Vater with irregular margins. Brush cytology obtained from the stricture is positive for adenocarcinoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ERCP and cytology confirm the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma at the ampulla of Vater. DIAGNOSIS READY: Ampullary carcinoma
